facts.text: Current Q7 (val:0007, 'clean some butterknife and put it in drawer.', both sides step_limit/50) step 25: before-state is at open drawer 1 showing knife 1 and spatula 1 (menu C29); action 'go to drawer 2'; after-state arrives at open empty drawer 2 (C31); feedback reward 0, admissible true, no fallback.

Historical S1_R04/Q6 ('put two candle in drawer.', success, 34 steps) step 25: before-state at open drawer 7 showing soapbar 2 (menu_244); action 'go to drawer 8'; after 'Nothing happens.'; feedback action_in_admissible_commands false.

answers.conditions: Both are index-25 steps under a 50-step limit, in different ALFRED tasks, scenes and skill iterations (current P7/Q7 vs S1_R04 P6/Q6 pairing).
answers.comparison: Q7:25 is an admissible productive navigation between drawers within one open-container search; S1_R04/Q6:25 issues a command absent from the menu, yielding a no-op. Same step number, different task, receptacles and admissible lists.
answers.conclusion: No paired or state-aligned relationship exists; the shared number 25 is coincidental. At most the two records contrast one admissible navigation against one inadmissible no-op in separate executions.
answers.uncertainty: No evidence aligns the two before-states; equal step indices do not identify equivalent states, and each run was executed once.

facts.text: P8 (task val:0008 'put a clean soapbar in cabinet.', step_limit/50), step 8: before-state at cabinet 1, open and empty (C48); action 'open cabinet 3'; after cabinet 3 opens and is empty (C53); feedback reward 0, admissible true, done false, fallback null.

P8:7 had just returned to the already-open empty cabinet 1. Menu C48 lists 'examine cabinet 3'/'open cabinet 3' but no 'go to cabinet 3'. The same pair also records inadmissible navigation attempts: P8:15 'go to cabinet 1' and Q8:39 'go to cabinet 3' both yielded 'Nothing happens.'

answers.conditions: Current pair P8/Q8; P8 uses the parent skill (no Admissible Actions section), Q8 the parent+diff skill. Cabinet 3 was empty when opened.
answers.comparison: With the desired destination 'go to cabinet 3' absent, P8:8 used the listed direct manipulation 'open cabinet 3' while standing at cabinet 1, exactly the pattern the added bullet describes; yet both P8 and Q8 elsewhere issued commands absent from their menus.
answers.conclusion: P8:8 exemplifies direct-action substitution when navigation is unavailable, but it occurs in the pre-guidance parent run, so it cannot be credited to the added text; the pair shows such behavior can arise from the environment menu alone, and admissibility was not reliably respected.
answers.uncertainty: Cannot isolate the guidance's effect: availability is environment-driven, both runs still attempted inadmissible commands, and the opened cabinet contained no target.

facts.text: The parent skill has the desklamp procedure and a general non-desklamp procedure (open closed containers, no substitute, clean-if-required, direct placement). The diff inserts a document-level '## Admissible Actions' section between the Constraints and the general procedure, and rewrites the general search steps 1-2 (open visible surfaces, no re-entering a just-left or cycling location, prefer untried receptacle types; similar category is not a substitute; leave non-matching contents).
P2/Q2 (val:0002, 'examine the pillow with the desklamp.') both succeed, 5 vs 6 steps; every recorded action is admissible, and both end by using the desklamp with the pillow carried to the desk.

answers.conditions: Pillow pair is a desklamp-conditioned inspection task; the search rewrite is scoped to the general non-desklamp procedure, while Admissible Actions sits globally.
answers.comparison: Neither pillow run contains an inadmissible command or substitute search, so neither changed clause is exercised; the only difference is one extra candidate navigation (Q2:1 desk first) before bed 1/bed 2.
answers.conclusion: The pillow pair lies outside the operative scope of both changes; it neither tests nor evidences them. The 5 vs 6 step gap is incidental exploration variation.
answers.uncertainty: Desklamp scope of Admissible Actions was not exercised; one trial per side, so efficiency claims are weak.

facts.text: P8 (parent, val:0008, 'put a clean soapbar in cabinet.') hit the 50-step limit, never observing a soapbar; it inspected cabinet 1 (empty), cabinet 2 (candle 2, soapbottle 2, spraybottle 2), cabinet 3 (empty), cabinet 4 (spraybottle 3), countertop 1 (candle 3) and sinkbasin 1 (empty), then cycled among cabinets 1-4.

Q8 (candidate) also hit the step limit with no soapbar; like P8 it checked cabinets 1-4, countertop 1 and sinkbasin 1, but additionally bathtubbasin 1 (empty) and sinkbasin 2 (empty). Neither run took or moved the visible soapbottle 2.

Historical Memory records that exact-target abstention and no-substitute behavior leave near-miss objects untouched but do not create success when the exact target is absent, and that cycling/step-limit failures persist.

answers.conditions: One run per side on the same scene; only cabinets 1-4, countertop 1 and sinkbasins were (partially) inspected.
answers.comparison: Candidate explored two extra receptacles (bathtubbasin, sinkbasin 2) but both executions repeatedly re-entered open, visibly empty cabinets; both left the non-target soapbottle unmanipulated.
answers.conclusion: Within inspected receptacles no soapbar was observed and neither execution satisfied the clean-soapbar placement; soapbottle 2 is not a substitute and was correctly left alone, but abstention produced no success, repeating the historical pattern.
answers.uncertainty: Absence from inspected containers is not global absence: shelf 1, toilet, garbagecan, towelholders and other surfaces were never inspected, and no independent verification exists.

facts.text: P10 (task val:0010, 'cool some apple and put it in microwave.') searched fridge, countertop 1, cabinet 1, countertop 2, returned to fridge and countertop 1, then diningtable; took apple 1; cooled it at the fridge while holding it; opened the microwave and moved the apple in; success in 14 steps.

Q10 covered fridge, countertop 1, countertop 2, diningtable directly; took apple 1; performed 'cool apple 1 with fridge 1' while holding it; then opened the microwave and moved the apple in; success in 11 steps. All actions in both runs were admissible.

answers.conditions: Current pair P10/Q10 (candidate uses parent+diff skill); both reward 1 on the final placement.
answers.comparison: Search differs by the parent's cabinet 1 detour plus extra fridge/countertop 1 revisits (3 extra navigation steps); acquisition of apple 1, holding-based cooling at the open fridge, and microwave opening/placement are preserved step-for-step.
answers.conclusion: Only search navigation changed, in the direction the revised anti-cycling/open-surface text prescribes, giving 11 vs 14 steps; conditioning and placement behavior is preserved. The Admissible Actions clause was not exercised, since neither run recorded an inadmissible command.
answers.uncertainty: One run per side; the three-step saving cannot be attributed to a specific clause, and both executions already succeeded.
